### 2. type-extraction-composition-constructor-coverage

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Confirmed in `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/TypeExtractionService.cs`. `InjectFieldAndCtorParameter` (lines 445-488) always injects a `private readonly {NewType} _field` (lines 448-454) but wires it through exactly ONE constructor: `typeDecl.Members.OfType<ConstructorDeclarationSyntax>().FirstOrDefault()` at line 456. Four broken construction topologies follow directly from that single line plus the body guard at line 481 (`if (updatedCtor.Body is not null)`): (1) **implicit constructor** — `existingCtor is null`, so the whole `if` block at 457-485 is skipped and the field is emitted with no parameter and no assignment; the preview compiles (unassigned readonly reference field is only CS8618/CS0649-class, not an error) so the breakage is SILENT — a permanently-null composition field. (2) **Overloaded constructors** — only the first declared ctor gains the parameter/assignment; every other ctor leaves the readonly field null, again silently. (3) **`this(...)`-chained constructors** — the first ctor's arity changes but the chained ctor's `: this(a, b)` argument list is untouched, producing CS1729 at apply time. (4) **Expression-bodied constructors** — the parameter IS added (lines 467-473) but line 481's `Body is not null` guard is false for `ExpressionBody`, so no assignment statement is ever added: the caller must now pass a value that is thrown away. The single call site is `PreviewExtractTypeAsync` line 100-102; the preview is stored and returned (lines 122-126) with no compile validation, so all four shapes reach the user as an apparently-clean diff. Static constructors and primary-constructor/record topologies are likewise unmodelled — a static ctor would be a candidate for `FirstOrDefault()` if declared first, and a primary constructor (`TypeDeclarationSyntax.ParameterList`) is invisible to the `OfType<ConstructorDeclarationSyntax>()` scan. |
| Approach | Single production file: `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/TypeExtractionService.cs`. Rewrite `InjectFieldAndCtorParameter` (lines 445-488) from a first-constructor mutation into a whole-topology pass, and give it the `sourceTypeName` argument it needs for refusal prose (update the sole call site at line 100). New shape: (a) **Classify** — enumerate all `ConstructorDeclarationSyntax` members, excluding static ctors (`StaticKeyword` modifier) from every mutation; treat a ctor whose `Initializer` is `ThisConstructorInitializer` as *chained* and everything else (no initializer, or `base(...)`) as *root*. (b) **Refuse unsupported topologies** before any syntax is emitted, mirroring the existing refusal idiom at lines 79-88 (`throw new InvalidOperationException($"Refusing to extract type '{newTypeName}' from '{sourceTypeName}': ...")`, already mapped by `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolErrorHandler.cs`): refuse when the source type declares a primary constructor (`typeDecl.ParameterList is not null`, covers `record`/`class C(...)`), and refuse any instance ctor with neither `Body` nor `ExpressionBody` (extern/partial). Each refusal names the offending topology and the remedy. (c) **Handle the supported set** — implicit (zero instance ctors): synthesize `public {SourceType}({NewType} p) { _field = p; }` via `SyntaxFactory.ConstructorDeclaration` and insert it after the field. Root ctors: add the parameter to EVERY root ctor (keeping the existing before-first-optional insertion logic at lines 467-473 — that is the BUG-005 CS1737 fix and must be preserved per-ctor) and append the assignment. Expression-bodied root ctors: rewrite to a block body — `SyntaxFactory.Block(ExpressionStatement(expressionBody.Expression), assignment)`, clearing `ExpressionBody` and the trailing semicolon token — instead of silently skipping (line 481). Chained ctors: add the parameter but NO assignment (the root it delegates to owns the single write of the readonly field); instead append the forwarded `IdentifierName(paramName)` argument to the `ThisConstructorInitializer`'s `ArgumentList`, matching the parameter's inserted position. (d) Replace all mutated ctors in one `typeDecl.ReplaceNodes(...)` call rather than the single `ReplaceNode` at line 484. |
| Scope | Production files: 1 — `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/TypeExtractionService.cs`. Test files: 1 (extended) — `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TypeExtractionTests.cs`. Files deleted: none. Changelog fragment `changelog.d/type-extraction-composition-constructor-coverage.md` (not counted). No Rule 3 exemption claimed — 1 of 4 production files. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |

Recommend a spin-off backlog row (`type-extraction-constructor-callsite-coverage`, ≤2 production files) rather than widening this initiative. ### 3. prompt-call-error-filter-boundary

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Every `get_prompt` handler swallows its own failures, so no shared protocol boundary ever observes a prompt exception. `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Prompts/PromptMessageBuilder.cs:36-44` (`CreateErrorMessage`) interpolates raw `ex.Message` into a `Role.User` `TextContentBlock` and returns it as a **successful** `prompts/get` result — a secret-bearing message (connection string, token, absolute path) inside an inner exception is published verbatim to the client, and the client cannot distinguish failure from content. ### 9. mcp-mrtr-dispatch-contract

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | The repo pins `ModelContextProtocol` 2.1.0 (`Directory.Packages.props:6`), whose MRTR surface is present and usable: `ModelContextProtocol.Protocol.InputRequiredException` (+ `InputRequiredResult.InputRequests` / `.RequestState`), `RequestParams.InputResponses`, `McpServer.IsMrtrSupported`, and `InputRequest.ForElicitation(...)` / `InputResponse.FromElicitResult(...)`. Nothing in `src/` references any of them — verified by ripgrep across `src/` (only `RequestProtocolFeatureGate` hits the protocol-era gate at all). Two concrete defects follow. **(1) MRTR is structurally impossible today.** `StructuredCallToolFilter.Create` wraps the whole dispatcher and its `catch (Exception ex)` at `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/StructuredCallToolFilter.cs:203` swallows every non-`OperationCanceledException` into `BuildErrorResult(...)` → `CallToolResult { IsError = true }` (`StructuredCallToolFilter.cs:479-488`). Only `OperationCanceledException` is rethrown (`:196-202`). So an `InputRequiredException` thrown by any handler inside `next(...)` never reaches the SDK's `McpServerImpl.InvokeWithInputRequiredResultHandlingAsync`; it is converted into a terminal tool error and the client sees a failed call instead of an input-required result. **(2) Server-driven input is stateful-only.** The only recovery path calls `context.Server!.ElicitAsync(...)` directly at `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/StructuredCallElicitationCoordinator.cs:106` and `:119`, then re-dispatches in-process (`:157`, `:237-242`). That is a nested-continuation shape that requires a stateful session; it has no MRTR-portable equivalent and nothing reads `RequestParams.InputResponses` on the retry request. Confirms the backlog row's Evidence exactly — the current mechanism catches binder failures and initiates a direct nested `ElicitAsync` continuation. |

### 10. analyzer-shadow-loader-lifecycle

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Anchors verified — all four cited paths exist and the described behavior still reproduces. `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/AnalyzerReferenceIsolation.cs:36` builds the shadow root as `Path.GetTempPath()/RoslynMcpAnalyzerShadow/<workspaceId>` and line 59 creates one `ShadowCopyAnalyzerAssemblyLoader` per analyzer path, but `RetargetFileReferencesToShadowLoader` returns only an `int` count (line 20/68) — the loaders and their `AssemblyLoadContext`s are handed to Roslyn via reflection (`AssemblyLoaderField.SetValue`, line 63) and then dropped on the floor. The load context is explicitly non-collectible: `ShadowAnalyzerLoadContext(...) : base(isCollectible: false)` at `AnalyzerReferenceIsolation.cs:246`, so nothing can ever unload it. The only caller is `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceSessionLoader.cs:77`, which discards everything but the count; `CreateAndOpenAsync` returns a bare `MSBuildWorkspace`. Consequently `WorkspaceSession` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceManager.cs:1242`) has no loader-lease field and its `Dispose` (line 1262) disposes only `Workspace` and `LoadLock` — so workspace close (line 495), the reload swap's `oldWorkspace?.Dispose()` (line 1055), the eviction path (lines 348/380/385), and host `Dispose` (line 866-883) all leak the ALC and leave the shadow tree on disk. That matches the detail file's evidence of 245–272 orphaned shadow trees / ~544–633 MB per full Release run. Second, latent defect: the shadow root is keyed by `workspaceId` ALONE, so a reload reuses the same directory — even once deletion exists, deleting on old-lease dispose would race the new lease's files. |
| Approach | Three production files, no new file. (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/AnalyzerReferenceIsolation.cs` — introduce a nested `public sealed class AnalyzerShadowLoaderLease : IDisposable` owning the per-load shadow root plus the created loaders/contexts, exposing `RetargetedReferenceCount`. Change `RetargetFileReferencesToShadowLoader` to return the lease (empty/no-op lease on the non-Windows and reflection-unavailable early returns at lines 25-34 so callers need no null checks). Make the shadow root per-LEASE, not per-workspace: `Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "RoslynMcpAnalyzerShadow", workspaceId, leaseId)` where `leaseId` is an `N`-format `Guid` — this is what makes old-lease deletion safe across a reload. Flip `ShadowAnalyzerLoadContext` to `base(isCollectible: true)` (line 246). Note that collectibility does NOT change `Assembly.Location`: loading stays `context.LoadFromAssemblyPath(ShadowCopy(...))` (lines 137/232), so shadow-copied analyzers keep a real on-disk `Location` and adjacent-resource/native probing behavior — the stream-loading shortcut the detail file rejects is explicitly NOT taken. `Dispose` calls `Unload()` on every context, then best-effort deletes the lease root with a bounded retry (a few attempts with `GC.Collect()` + `GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers()` between, since ALC unload is asynchronous and mapped files stay locked until collection completes); a still-undeletable root is logged at Debug and left for the sweeper. Add a static `SweepAbandonedRoots(ILogger)` that deletes stale `RoslynMcpAnalyzerShadow/<workspaceId>/<leaseId>` directories not owned by a live lease (mirror the abandoned-run reaper discipline in `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestInfrastructure/TestTempRoot.cs` — never delete the shared parent, never delete a live sibling). Dispose must be idempotent (release exactly once). (2) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceSessionLoader.cs` — change `CreateAndOpenAsync` to return `(MSBuildWorkspace Workspace, AnalyzerReferenceIsolation.AnalyzerShadowLoaderLease Lease)`, keeping the existing catch block's ownership contract: on throw-before-return, dispose the lease alongside `workspace.Dispose()` (line 95). (3) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceManager.cs` — add `AnalyzerShadowLoaderLease? AnalyzerLease { get; set; }` to `WorkspaceSession` (line 1242) and release it in `WorkspaceSession.Dispose` (line 1262) after `Workspace?.Dispose()`, which covers close (line 495), eviction (lines 348/380/385) and host `Dispose` (line 883). In `LoadIntoSessionAsync`, capture the lease at the call site (line 979), mirror the existing atomic-swap pattern exactly: assign `session.AnalyzerLease = newLease` in the same post-load block as `session.Workspace = newWorkspace` (line ~1026), and in the `finally` dispose the OLD lease alongside `oldWorkspace?.Dispose()` on the swapped path (line 1055) / the NEW lease alongside `newWorkspace?.Dispose()` on the failure path (line 1064). Lease disposal always follows workspace disposal so Roslyn has released the analyzer references first. |
| Scope | Production files (3): `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/AnalyzerReferenceIsolation.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceSessionLoader.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceManager.cs`. Within Rule 3's 4-file cap — no exemption claimed. Test files (3, at the Rule 4 cap): NEW `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/AnalyzerShadowLoaderLifecycleTests.cs` (Windows-gated lifecycle regression); `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceSessionLoaderFailureTests.cs` (compile-forced — `ThrowAfterFirstCallLoader.CreateAndOpenAsync` override at line 75 must adopt the new return type); `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/UnresolvedAnalyzerReferenceStripperTests.cs` (compile-forced — two `using var msbuildWorkspace = await loader.CreateAndOpenAsync(...)` call sites at lines 40 and 86 must destructure the tuple). No files deleted. `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ValidationIntegrationTests.cs` is deliberately NOT touched: it drives `WorkspaceManager`, not `CreateAndOpenAsync`, and its loader-type assertion (line 108) must keep passing unmodified as the compatibility witness. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 55000 |
| Risks | (1) `AssemblyLoadContext.Unload()` is asynchronous — the shadow tree may still be locked when `Dispose` returns; deletion is therefore best-effort with retry plus a sweeper, and the regression must assert reclamation with a bounded wait rather than a synchronous check, or it will be flaky. (2) Collectible ALCs throw on unload if an analyzer leaks a rooted reference (static caches, timers, `AssemblyLoadContext.Default` cross-links via the `Resolve` fallback at line 217). Failure must be contained: log and fall through to the sweeper, never let a third-party analyzer's leak fault workspace close. (3) `Assembly.Location` and adjacent-resource behavior are the load-bearing compatibility property — verify explicitly that `isCollectible: true` with path-loading preserves a non-empty `Location`; do not "simplify" to `LoadFromStream`. (4) `WorkspaceManager.cs` is an addenda-listed hotspot (330+ lines of shared workspace state) — do not schedule this in the same parallel wave as another `WorkspaceManager.cs`-touching initiative, and keep the edit strictly inside the existing atomic-swap block so the `autoreload-cascade-stdio-host-crash` invariant (readers see prior-or-new, never half-initialized) is preserved. (5) Double-release: eviction, explicit close, and host `Dispose` can all reach the same session — lease disposal must be idempotent. (6) The lease-id subdirectory changes the on-disk shadow layout; any external cleanup expecting `RoslynMcpAnalyzerShadow/<workspaceId>/<hash>` sees one more level. Fanout probe was run (shape A, signature change) — see below. |

### 11. publish-tag-version-parity

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | The publish workflow validates internal version-file parity but never compares the release provenance (pushed tag / GitHub release name) with it. `.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml:42-44` runs `./eng/verify-release.ps1 -Configuration Release -NoCoverage -RequireConsumedFragments`, which invokes `eng/verify-version-drift.ps1` (`eng/verify-release.ps1:107-112`) to assert the six version files agree with the canonical `Directory.Build.props` `<Version>` (`eng/verify-version-drift.ps1:26-98`). Nothing reads `github.ref_name` or `github.event.release.tag_name` in that job. Two concrete consequences of a mistag: (1) `dotnet nuget push … --skip-duplicate` (`publish-nuget.yml:96-99`) silently no-ops when the canonical version was already published, so a wrong tag produces a green run with no package; (2) the downstream `publish-registry` job resolves its version FROM the tag — `v="${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}"` / `v="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"`, `v="${v#v}"` (`publish-nuget.yml:131-141`) — and then polls `https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/darylmcd.roslynmcp/$ver/readme` (`publish-nuget.yml:144-161`), so a tag that disagrees with the packed version either times out after ~20 min or publishes registry provenance pointing at a version the pack step never produced. The trigger filter `v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+` (`publish-nuget.yml:6-8`) constrains tag SHAPE only, never its VALUE; the `release` trigger has no shape filter at all. |
| Approach | Add one deterministic pre-build gate and wire it into the publish job. (1) New `eng/verify-publish-version-context.ps1` — mirror the parameterized, standalone-runnable shape of `eng/verify-breaking-version-bump.ps1:16-24` (`[CmdletBinding()]`, explicit params, `[string]$RepoRoot = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..')).Path`, `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`, exit 0/1 with a `VERSION DRIFT`-style error block copied in spirit from `eng/verify-version-drift.ps1:87-98`). Params: `-EventName` (`push`\|`release`\|`workflow_dispatch`, `[ValidateSet]`), `-RefName`, `-ReleaseTag`, `-RepoRoot`. Behavior: read canonical `<Version>` from `Directory.Build.props` exactly as `verify-version-drift.ps1:26-34` does; for `push` normalize `$RefName`, for `release` normalize `$ReleaseTag`, stripping a single leading `v` and requiring `^v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` (malformed or empty on a tag/release event → exit 1 with the offending literal echoed); compare to canonical, exit 1 on mismatch naming both values; for `workflow_dispatch` skip the comparison entirely and print the canonical version (manual dry-run must not need to invent a tag). (2) `.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml` — insert a `Verify release provenance` step in the `publish` job immediately AFTER `Set up .NET` and BEFORE `Verify release build` (i.e. between lines 34-40 and line 42), `shell: pwsh`, running `./eng/verify-publish-version-context.ps1 -EventName '${{ github.event_name }}' -RefName '${{ github.ref_name }}' -ReleaseTag '${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}'`. Because `publish-registry` declares `needs: publish` (`publish-nuget.yml:117`), failing here also blocks the tag-derived registry publish — no second wiring point needed. (3) New `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/PublishVersionContextTests.cs` — one event-context matrix driving the real script out-of-process, mirroring `ChangelogFragmentRequirementTests.RunVerifierAsync` (`tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ChangelogFragmentRequirementTests.cs:290-322`: `ProcessStartInfo` with `pwsh.exe`/`pwsh`, `-NoProfile -File <script> -RepoRoot <fixtureRoot>`, redirected stdout/stderr, 30s `CancellationTokenSource` kill-on-timeout), plus a workflow-contract assertion in the style of `BreakingVersionGateTests.cs:53-63` that the new step's index in `publish-nuget.yml` precedes both `- name: Verify release build` and `- name: Pack NuGet package`. |
| Scope | Production files (2): `.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml` (modified — one new step), `eng/verify-publish-version-context.ps1` (new). Test files added (1): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/PublishVersionContextTests.cs` (new). Files deleted: none. No Rule 3 exemption claimed or needed — 2 ≤ 4. Confirmed NOT release-managed: the guard's exact-match set is `Directory.Build.props`, `manifest.json`, `.claude-plugin/{plugin,marketplace,server}.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `eng/verify-version-drift.ps1`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `eng/verify-skills-are-generic.ps1` (`eng/guard-release-managed-files.ps1:54-64`), so neither touched file trips the PreToolUse block or needs the `.release-managed-edit-allowed` sentinel. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 35000 |
| Risks | (1) `github.event.release.tag_name` is empty on `push` and `workflow_dispatch` events, so the script must accept an empty `-ReleaseTag` on those paths and only hard-fail when the event is `release` — getting this backwards breaks every tag push. (2) YAML quoting: the `${{ }}` expansions must be single-quoted in the pwsh `run:` block or a tag containing unexpected characters injects into the command line. (3) Adjacent behavior to verify — `BreakingVersionGateTests.cs:53-63` already asserts ordering inside `publish-nuget.yml` (`verify-release.ps1 -RequireConsumedFragments` before `- name: Pack NuGet package`); inserting the new step BEFORE the verify-release step preserves both index comparisons, but re-run that test. (4) Fanout probe (contract sites, not edit sites): a repo-wide grep for `verify-version-drift.ps1` returns 10 files — `CHANGELOG.md`, `justfile`, `ai_docs/workflow.md`, `docs/upgrade-matrix.md`, `docs/release-policy.md`, `eng/verify-release.ps1`, `eng/guard-release-managed-files.ps1`, `ai_docs/items/workflow-md-release-managed-guard-list-drift.md`, `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/BreakingVersionGateTests.cs`, `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/VerifyReleaseChildScriptTests.cs` — showing the doc/justfile surface an analogous gate accretes over time. The new script deliberately does NOT join `verify-release.ps1`'s child-script chain (it is publish-event-scoped, not a merge gate), so none of those 10 sites are forced edits; `docs/release-policy.md` is the one optional follow-up and is left out to hold the 2-file scope. (5) `eng/publish-nuget.ps1` (the manual publish path) gets no provenance gate here — that file is the scope of the sibling `manual-nuget-publish-provenance` initiative; do not edit it in this PR. No anchors were stale: `.github/workflows/publish-nuget.yml` verified present; the other two anchors are declared-new files. |
| Validation | (a) `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PublishVersionContextTests"` (or `mcp__roslyn__test_run --filter PublishVersionContextTests`) covering the required matrix: `push` with matching tag → exit 0; `push` with mismatched tag → exit 1 naming both versions; `release` with matching `tag_name` → exit 0; `release` with mismatched `tag_name` → exit 1; malformed input (`refs/heads/main`, `v3.0`, empty string on a tag event) → exit 1; `workflow_dispatch` with no tag → exit 0 and no comparison performed. ### 12. manual-nuget-publish-provenance

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `eng/publish-nuget.ps1` (62 lines, verified live) pushes an unvalidated, unbuilt artifact. (a) `param([string]$Version…)` at line 2 plus lines 37-43 accept ANY caller-supplied version and only fall back to `Directory.Build.props` when omitted — no comparison to the canonical six-file state that `eng/verify-version-drift.ps1` owns. (b) Lines 45-48 select a PRE-EXISTING `nupkg\$PackageId.$Version.nupkg` by filename alone — no pack, no build/test gate, no package-content assertion; a months-old nupkg left in `nupkg/` from an earlier release is pushed verbatim. | Field | Content |

The two gates therefore execute the same suite on disjoint operating systems, and nothing between merge and tag re-runs it on Linux — the v3.0.1 hole. The three v3.0.1 casualties still exist and are now Linux-safe: `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/NuGetAuditGateTests.cs:13` reads lowercase `"justfile"` with a comment naming the case-sensitivity trap, and `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestInfrastructure/PowerShellOutputNormalizer.cs` is consumed by `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/BreakingVersionGateTests.cs` and `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/VerifyReleaseChildScriptTests.cs` to neutralize width-dependent `Write-Error` wrapping. ### 14. tool-call-error-envelope-wire-contract

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | The `tools/call` error envelope is only covered in-process. `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/StructuredCallToolFilterTests.cs:117-131` calls the `internal` helper `StructuredCallToolFilter.BuildErrorResult` directly and asserts `category: InternalError`, absence of `exceptionType`/`stackTrace`, and presence of `correlationId` — it never serializes a JSON-RPC frame, so it cannot prove where the envelope lands on the wire (`result` vs protocol `error`), whether `isError` survives serialization, whether application `_meta` is accidentally promoted to the protocol result `_meta`, or whether the era discriminator `resultType` appears. The redaction shape it half-covers is produced by `ToolErrorHandler.FormatErrorResponse` at `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolErrorHandler.cs:574-614`: the `InternalError` branch (lines 576-586) emits exactly `{error, category, tool, message, correlationId}` — deliberately dropping the `exceptionType` field that the generic `BuildErrorEnvelope` path adds at line 563 — and `schemaHint` is attached only for `InvalidArgument` (line 607-612), so it must be absent for an unexpected `InternalError`. The existing raw-wire suite `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/StructuredContentWireContractTests.cs` asserts `IsError is false` for every case it drives (line 158-160), confirming the backlog evidence that the dirty-wire coverage is success-path only. Nothing pins the serialized failure frame end-to-end. |
| Approach | Add one new test file `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ToolCallErrorWireContractTests.cs`, mirroring the structure of `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ProtocolVersionResultShapeWireTests.cs` almost exactly — it is the closest existing template: a private `[McpServerToolType]` nested class registered via `.WithTools<T>()`, `.WithRequestFilters(filters => filters.AddCallToolFilter(StructuredCallToolFilter.Create))`, a provider-built `McpServerOptions`, and `InMemoryMcpClientServerHarness.CreateAsync(..., protocolVersion: <era>, captureServerMessages: true)`. Reuse its `FindSingleNewResult(harness.RawServerMessages, priorMessageCount)` helper shape verbatim (`ProtocolVersionResultShapeWireTests.cs:115-129`) to pull the single raw response frame, and extend it to also capture frames carrying a JSON-RPC `error` member so the test can assert that member is absent. The synthetic tool throws one unexpected, nested exception (e.g. `new InvalidOperationException("outer", new NullReferenceException("sentinel <SECRET-SENTINEL> at C:\\local\\path"))` — deliberately not one of the classified shapes in `ToolErrorHandler`, so it routes to the `InternalError` branch at `ToolErrorHandler.cs:576`). Parameterize over the two supported eras already used repo-wide (`"2025-11-25"` requested and `null` → `"2026-07-28"`), matching `StructuredContentWireContractTests.cs:29-51`. Assertions, per the detail file's `## Acceptance`: raw frame has a `result` member and no `error` member; `result.isError == true`; exactly one `content` block of type `text`; `content[0].text` parses as JSON with `category == "InternalError"`, a `correlationId`, and an application `_meta` block; `schemaHint` absent; the protocol-level `result._meta` does not carry the application `_meta`/`schemaHint` fields; legacy era omits `resultType` while the modern era carries `resultType: "complete"`; and a raw-string scan of the whole serialized frame proves absence of the secret sentinel, the exception type names, the inner message, `at RoslynMcp.` stack frames, and the local path fragment. No production file changes. |

### 1.01. resource-read-protocol-error-semantics-workspace

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Split from `resource-read-protocol-error-semantics` per Rule 4 — 1-of-2 parts. Every MCP resource handler wraps its body in `ToolErrorHandler.ExecuteResource` / `ExecuteResourceAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolErrorHandler.cs:141` and `:175`). Both catch `Exception`, call `ClassifyError` + `FormatErrorResponse`, and RETURN the serialized error document as the resource body (`ToolErrorHandler.cs:168`, `:206`) — so a JSON-RPC `resources/read` for a missing workspace answers with a SUCCESS result whose single `contents` entry is `{"error":true,"category":"NotFound", ...}`. This confirms the backlog evidence verbatim. There are 10 wrapped call sites: 7 in `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Resources/WorkspaceResources.cs` (lines 18, 28, 46, 60, 74, 96, 238 — two sync, five async) and 3 in `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Resources/ServerResources.cs` (lines 49, 67, 85, all sync). The registered read boundary `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/ResourceReadResultFilter.cs:15-28` (wired at `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Program.cs:84`) currently only stamps `TimeToLive`/`CacheScope` and has no `try`/`catch`, so no exception ever reaches the SDK failure channel. Protocol selection already exists per-request at `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/RequestProtocolFeatureGate.cs:14-24` (reads `context.JsonRpcRequest.Context?.ProtocolVersion` then `context.Server.NegotiatedProtocolVersion` — never static/session-cached), which is the era selector the acceptance criteria ask for. **Split rationale (Rule 4):** stripping the catch from the shared wrapper in one commit force-breaks FIVE existing test files that assert the body-envelope shape off direct handler calls — `ErrorResponseObservabilityTests.cs:140,155`, `Top10V2RegressionTests.cs:93,112,129`, `FetchMcpResourceReadinessTests.cs:131-144`, `SurfaceCatalogTests.cs:221-225`, plus the new wire-matrix file = 6 test files against a cap of 3. The two resource families are independently migratable because each call site names its wrapper explicitly, so this part migrates the WorkspaceResources family only. **Stale anchor:** the acceptance criterion citing `McpProtocolVersions.UseInvalidParamsForMissingResource(protocol)` does not resolve — the SDK's `McpProtocolVersions` helper is `internal` and unavailable to server filters (documented at `RequestProtocolFeatureGate.cs:21`), and no such member exists in this repo. |
| Approach | Four production edits, additive-then-migrate so the tree compiles and stays green at every step. (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolErrorHandler.cs` — ADD success-only siblings `ExecuteResourceScope(string source, Func<string> action)` and `ExecuteResourceScopeAsync(string source, Func<Task<string>> action)`: keep the `AmbientGateMetrics.BeginRequest()` scope, the stopwatch, and `InjectMetaIfPossible` on the success path; move the `metrics.ElapsedMs` write into a `finally` so failed reads still record elapsed time; NO `catch` arm — every exception propagates. The legacy catching `ExecuteResource` / `ExecuteResourceAsync` overloads stay in place untouched for the three not-yet-migrated `ServerResources.cs` sites (part 2 deletes them). The new names also retire the naming smell where `ExecuteResource*` keeps its name while losing its error-handling role. (2) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/RequestProtocolFeatureGate.cs` — add `public static bool UseInvalidParamsForMissingResource<TParams>(RequestContext<TParams> context) => SupportsJuly2026Features(context);` as the single named era selector (the acceptance criterion's `McpProtocolVersions` name is unavailable; this is the local equivalent) so no filter duplicates a protocol-string comparison. (3) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/ResourceReadResultFilter.cs` — wrap `await next(context, cancellationToken)` in `try`/`catch`, rethrow `OperationCanceledException`, and translate everything else into `McpException` using the existing internal `ToolErrorHandler.ClassifyError(ex, uriTemplateOrUri)` for the sanitized category/remediation text: categories `NotFound` / `FileNotFound` / `DirectoryNotFound` / `WorkspaceEvicted` map to `McpErrorCode.ResourceNotFound` (-32002), or to `McpErrorCode.InvalidParams` (-32602) when `UseInvalidParamsForMissingResource(context)` is true; `InvalidArgument` maps to `InvalidParams` in both eras; everything else maps to sanitized `McpErrorCode.InternalError` (-32603). Carry only `ErrorInfo.Category`, its remediation `Message`, `ParamName`, the requested URI, and the correlation id — never exception type, stack, raw path, or `ex.Message`. Keep the existing `Normalize(...)` caching stamp on the success path untouched (that contract is locked by `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ServerDiscoveryWireTests.cs:331`). (4) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Resources/WorkspaceResources.cs` — mechanical switch of all 7 call sites (18, 28 → `ExecuteResourceScope`; 46, 60, 74, 96, 238 → `ExecuteResourceScopeAsync`) and refresh the stale comment at `:222`. |
| Scope | Production files (4): `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolErrorHandler.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/ResourceReadResultFilter.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/RequestProtocolFeatureGate.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Resources/WorkspaceResources.cs`. At the Rule 3 base cap of 4 — no exemption claimed. Test files (3, all MODIFIED, none new): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ErrorResponseObservabilityTests.cs` (the two direct-call resource tests at lines 140 and 155 flip from asserting an error envelope to asserting the exception propagates; the stale comment at `:138` is corrected), `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/Top10V2RegressionTests.cs` (the three `SourceFileLines` invalid-argument tests at lines 93, 112, 129 flip the same way; stale comment at `:84` corrected), `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/FetchMcpResourceReadinessTests.cs` (`WorkspaceStatusResource_UnknownWorkspace_ReturnsStructuredNotFound` at lines 131-144 flips to asserting propagation; the three success-path tests at 61, 81, 113 are unchanged). At the Rule 4 cap of 3 — no further test file may be touched in this part. `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceResourceTests.cs` was inspected and needs NO change (success shapes plus an already-throwing case at line 148); `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WindowsPathResourceTests.cs` and `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceToolsIntegrationTests.cs` call resources only on success paths. `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/SurfaceCatalogTests.cs` is deliberately deferred to part 2 (it exercises the ServerResources family). No files deleted. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 55000 |
| Risks | (a) Removing the catch drops the `_meta`/metrics injection that previously rode on the FAILURE path — the `finally` placement for `AmbientGateMetrics.ElapsedMs` is load-bearing; verify a failed read still records elapsed time. (b) The success-path caching contract in `ServerDiscoveryWireTests` must stay green — do not restructure `Normalize`. (c) Two wrapper families coexist until part 2 lands (`ExecuteResourceScope*` success-only, `ExecuteResource*` legacy-catching) — that duplication is intentional and time-boxed; part 2 deletes the legacy pair. (d) The stale `McpProtocolVersions.UseInvalidParamsForMissingResource` acceptance anchor is satisfied by a locally-named equivalent on `RequestProtocolFeatureGate`; if a reviewer insists on the SDK symbol, it is `internal` and unreachable. (e) BREAKING wire change for clients that parse the error document out of `contents` on workspace resources — migration guidance required in the changelog fragment. (f) The detail file's `deps: tool-error-envelope-sensitive-detail-disclosure` names an id with no open row in `ai_docs/backlog.md` (it appears only in other rows' deps cells), so the dependency reads as already satisfied. (g) Fanout probe: `grep -rn ExecuteResource --include=*.cs` returns exactly 3 production files (`ToolErrorHandler.cs`, `WorkspaceResources.cs`, `ServerResources.cs`) plus 2 test files whose only hits are comments; this part touches 2 of those 3 plus the 2 middleware files = 4, matching `productionFilesTouched`. |
| Validation | `mcp__roslyn__compile_check` after each edit. Targeted: `mcp__roslyn__test_run --filter "ErrorResponseObservabilityTests"`, then `Top10V2RegressionTests`, `FetchMcpResourceReadinessTests`, `WorkspaceResourceTests`, `WindowsPathResourceTests`, `WorkspaceToolsIntegrationTests`, `ServerDiscoveryWireTests`, `StaticListResultFilterTests`, `SurfaceCatalogTests` (must stay green — the ServerResources family is untouched here). Manual repro: drive raw JSON-RPC `resources/read` for `roslyn://workspace/ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff/status` and assert the response carries a top-level `error` object (code -32002 under `2025-11-25`, -32602 under `2026-07-28`) with NO `result.contents`; repeat with `roslyn://workspace/{id}/file/{path}/lines/10-5` expecting -32602 in both eras, and assert no error payload contains an exception type name, stack frame, or absolute path. Full gate: `./eng/verify-release.ps1 -Configuration Release` plus `./eng/verify-ai-docs.ps1`. |
| Performance review | N/A — correctness fix, no hot-path changes. |
| CHANGELOG category | Changed — BREAKING |
| CHANGELOG entry (draft) | **Changed — BREAKING:** `resources/read` failures on workspace resources (`roslyn://workspaces*`, `roslyn://workspace/**`) now travel over the JSON-RPC error channel instead of being serialized into a successful `contents` body. Missing workspaces/files return `-32002` (`ResourceNotFound`) under protocol `2025-11-25` and `-32602` (`InvalidParams`) under `2026-07-28`; malformed line ranges return `-32602` in both eras; unexpected handler failures return a sanitized `-32603`. Error payloads carry only a stable category, remediation text, the requested resource URI, and a correlation id — never exception types, stack traces, or raw paths. **Migration:** clients that parsed `{"error":true,"category":...}` out of the resource body must read the JSON-RPC `error` member instead. Server-catalog resources follow in the next release. |
